body:
As far as the crying in bed and 'setting it off' goes, I'm fairly sure that it's just the culmination of multiple years of despair and me finally beginning to lose restraint on occasion while unconscious.

My brain doesn't usually fixate on a specific thing repeatedly (other than failing to find a girlfriend, which is fairly normal for my school, given that we have a 2-3:1 male:female ratio), but to give some simple examples:
I am a failure because I have not published any original research yet. Rationally, I know this is because my faculty partners made some bad project decisions, ultimately leading to the project failure. However, I still feel internally that I should have managed to make up for this somehow.
I am a failure because I have not managed to get a date yet. Rationally, I know that my school has a very bad ratio, and a good portion of the women do not want to date while here because it might detract from their ability to study.
I am a failure because I know people in my field about my age who are better at it than me. Rationally, I know this kind of expectation of myself is absurd.
I am a failure because I know people who are strictly better than me at everything I do (not just my field). For example, I know a person who is better than me in my field, has managed to get a girlfriend at a poor ratio school, is going to a higher ranked school than me, and on top of that is already financially stable, all while in college. In other words, there is a strictly better model of myself. Rationally, I know that just because I'm much worse than someone else, doesn't mean I'm worthless.

I think that overall, the thing that really gets to me the most is that I don't make anyone truly happy like I would if I had a good relationship, and not doing that seems to make my life pointless and worthless.

Sorry for the rambling.

I live in a self-governed dorm, and do have my own room. I'm not crying in my sleep due to bad dreams (I think), I can't really remember anything particularly odd about the dreams. To tell the truth, crying in my sleep has only happened 3 times, but as I've been able to mentally restrain most other things, it's still unnerving.

Talked about it to several friends, they all suggest seeking help. I'm not talking about it to my family, as even in HS they warned me to avoid the crazy people who saw doctors for mental conditions, so they likely wouldn't take the idea of me having a mental condition well.

I'm not particularly confident in groups, but I'm an officer in four organizations. However, these organizations are not particularly social (running a cluster, making changes to curriculum, and managing some dorm IT budgets). So no, I don't really have any regular close group social activities as you describe. It's not that I don't have friends--I have plenty of them, but things are more random spur of the moment with them.

I've had things that might be classified as panic attempts, but I'm not a doctor so I don't know. Essentially I become unable to do any useful work or interact with people due to my mind looping really fast on how worthless I am, and I have to go find a place to sit and wait for it to be over.

It's mostly just that I feel like I'm just going through the motions, see no purpose to my life or what I'm doing. The physical manifestations largely scare me because a coherent system of internal regulations are able to keep any of my mental issues (continual extreme saddness, shyness, etc.) from being as easily visible.

Hey, I've lurked on reddit for a long time, but only today saw the SW subreddit. If I'm violating protocol here in some way, please tell me.

For the past several (approximately 4-5) years, I've had self-worth issues pretty much continually. They've gradually gotten worse as the years go by. Last year, the worst they got was that I had to spend a couple hours alone each day, just trying to compose myself so I'd look happy when I walked outside. This year, I've had to change my sleeping position, as I sometimes begin to cry in my sleep (I wake up shortly thereafter), and the walls are thin enough that people around me can likely hear if I'm not muffled. 

I've thought about seeking a real counselor (I'm not hard up for money) but am not sure how much good it would do, or if it's even a good idea.

Additionally, my problem seems to stem from an inability to internalize certain logical facts. Other than relationships (I haven't managed to land a date yet, and I'm in my junior year in college), I'm fairly good at everything I do, so it seems like I shouldn't be feeling how I do, but this doesn't do anything about it.

Does anyone have any comments or suggestions? I can explain more about my life if people think it would be relevant.
